points.description: Identifies the article's organization as a logical progression from general to specific, or from problem to causes, examples and consequences. Equivalent descriptions earn the mark, such as: an opening hook, then a definition and history of space junk, then examples of collisions and accidents, then the dangers and possible solutions. Naming the sections (What Is Space Junk?, Crash Course, Little Bits, But a Big Deal) also counts.

Supports the description with specific details from the article, such as at least two of: the opening comet/tool-bag hook; the chronological history beginning with the 1957 Soviet satellite; the February 2009 satellite collision; the 2008 lost tool bag; the sandblaster comparison; the closing note on future cooperation. Accurate references to the text earn the mark. Vague claims with no textual support do not.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for a clear description of the article's structure, such as general-to-specific or problem-to-causes-to-solutions, backed by specific accurate details from the text. One mark for a correct structure with little or no support, or for listing details without explaining how they are organized. Zero for an incorrect or missing description of the organization.
